title: Day-trader mode: walk-forward historical signal replay (analyse_history) over intraday data
description:
Follow-up split out of backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine's own `decisions` entry: that task genericized `app.signals.engine.analyse()`'s single-point-in-time evaluation (via the new `analyse_day_trader()` entry point) and gave `_long_term_through_bar_date` (renamed from `_weekly_through_bar_date`) a `long_term_unit` parameter with a working `DAY`/`MINUTE` branch, but deliberately did not build day-trader-mode support for `app.signals.engine.analyse_history()` -- the walk-forward, per-bar historical replay that powers `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators`'s chart overlay for swing mode.

`app.data.day_trader_intraday.get_intraday_bars_for_triple`/`get_active_day_trader_intraday_bars` only ever fetch 'the most recent N days of bars, as of now' -- the right shape for a live signal computation, but not for a growing walk-forward replay over historical intraday data the way `analyse_history` does for swing mode (precomputing indicator series once over the full history, then slicing per bar). Building this needs a genuinely new IBKR historical-fetch design: paginating backward through a much longer intraday history window while still respecting `IBKRProvider`'s own per-call pagination bounds (`_MAX_PAGINATION_PAGES`/`_MAX_BARS_PER_PAGE`), and deciding what 'look-ahead' means for a bar-by-bar replay across three intraday legs resampled at different multiples of the same underlying feed.

This is genuinely optional/lower-priority relative to the other day-trader-mode follow-ups: a day-trader-mode chart-overlay history view is a real feature gap, but the live single-signal computation (`analyse_day_trader`, already built) is the more fundamental capability, and `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api` doesn't strictly need this to expose a live day-trader-mode analysis endpoint.

checklist.step: Design the IBKR historical-fetch shape needed for a growing walk-forward replay over intraday bars (pagination strategy, how far back to fetch, how to respect IBKR's own pagination bounds) -- record the design and rejected alternatives via `decisions`.

Decide what 'no look-ahead' means for a per-bar replay across three intraday legs resampled at different multiples of the same underlying feed, and how `_long_term_through_bar_date`'s `MINUTE`/`DAY` branch (already built) fits into it.

Wire day-trader-mode support into `analyse_history()` (or a new day-trader-mode-specific equivalent), with the same precompute-and-slice performance discipline the swing-mode implementation already uses.
Unit/integration tests, including a mocked IBKR intraday provider exercising a real multi-bar walk-forward replay end to end (no live network call).
Update docs/architecture/Backend.md §10's 'Not yet landed' list accordingly.

decisions.decision: No *new* IBKR-side pagination logic was built. `IBKRProvider.get_hourly_bars` already paginates backward across as many pages as needed (bounded only by its own pre-existing `_MAX_PAGINATION_PAGES`=20 / `_MAX_BARS_PER_PAGE`=1000 safety bound) for whatever `lookback_days` it's given -- the 'genuinely new IBKR historical-fetch design' this task's own `description` calls for turned out to be a *data-fetch-shape* problem, not a pagination-mechanics one: a new public helper, `app.data.ibkr_provider.max_lookback_days_for_bar_size(bar_size)`, computes the maximum calendar days of history achievable at a given IBKR-native granularity from those same three existing constants, and `app.data.day_trader_intraday.get_intraday_history_bars_for_triple` (a new sibling of the existing live-snapshot `get_intraday_bars_for_triple`, sharing its concurrent fan-out/fan-in via a newly-extracted `_fetch_legs_concurrently` helper) uses it to clamp its own much-larger default `lookback_days` (90, vs. the live-snapshot fetch's 30) *per leg* down to whatever that leg's own chosen IBKR-native bar size can actually return. `get_active_day_trader_intraday_history_bars` mirrors the existing trading-mode-setting-driven `get_active_day_trader_intraday_bars` for symmetry, even though no route calls it yet.
decisions.rationale: Confirmed directly against `get_hourly_bars`'s own implementation and its existing regression test (`TestGetHourlyBars.test_stops_at_the_page_safety_bound_when_cutoff_is_never_reached`, which already proves it terminates at exactly 20 pages/20,000 bars for a pathologically large `lookback_days`) before writing anything -- it already self-limits correctly regardless of what `lookback_days` a caller passes, since the `_MAX_PAGINATION_PAGES` loop simply stops issuing further requests once the page cap is hit. That means clamping upstream changes no actual fetched data (the two are mathematically equivalent for what bars come back); the value it adds is purely informational -- a caller can know in advance how much history a specific leg's own granularity can ever honor, rather than silently discovering fewer bars came back than requested with no way to tell why. Revisiting `_MAX_PAGINATION_PAGES`/`_MAX_BARS_PER_PAGE` themselves (raising the actual achievable-history ceiling for a feature that needs deep finer-grained history) was considered and rejected as out of scope here -- `get_hourly_bars`'s own docstring already flagged that as a distinct, unscoped problem before this task existed ('a day-trader-mode feature that actually needs deep finer-grained history would need to revisit that bound, out of scope here'), and this task's own `description` frames it as 'genuinely optional/lower-priority', not the moment to take on a larger, riskier change to a shared, already-reviewed pagination loop every other IBKR-dependent feature in this app also depends on. The 90-day default (not, say, `max_lookback_days_for_bar_size`'s own per-leg maximum) was chosen as 'enough for a meaningful chart without requesting far more than most legs' finer granularities could ever honor anyway' -- a future API-layer caller (`backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups`) wanting a specific chart `range` should pass its own `lookback_days` explicitly rather than relying on this default.

decisions.decision: 'No look-ahead' for the walk-forward replay is defined as: every one of the three legs' own bar timestamps is treated as its 'knowable as of' point, uniformly across all three legs -- i.e. `long_term_ohlcv`/`short_term_ohlcv` are both truncated to `index <= bar_date` (via `_long_term_through_bar_date`'s pre-existing `MINUTE` branch, unmodified, and a new sibling `_short_term_through_bar_date` that delegates to the exact same branch) at every one of `analyse_history_day_trader`'s per-`intermediate_ohlcv`-bar replay steps. Two more precise alternatives were considered and rejected: (1) computing each intermediate bar's own *settlement instant* (`bar_date` + that leg's own bar width) and using that, instead of `bar_date` itself, as the truncation cutoff for the other two legs; (2) exact interval-overlap checking (only including a coarser-leg bar once its own end has fully elapsed relative to the driving bar's start, computed from each leg's real bar width).
decisions.rationale: Both raw IBKR bars and this app's own client-side resampling (`app.data.base.resample_ohlcv`'s default `label="left"`) label a bar by its *start*, not its close -- so a bar labeled `T` isn't literally 'settled' until `T` + that leg's own bar width, and the uniform `<= bar_date` rule is a deliberate, documented approximation, not a claim otherwise. Alternative (1) was rejected because it only meaningfully matters for the long_term leg (the only one wider than intermediate, by `TimeframeTriple`'s own hard ordering rule), and even there the practical effect is at most a one-bar boundary edge case for any triple reasonably close to ch. 39's own factor-of-five guideline -- while the arithmetic needs a genuine trading-calendar-aware 'add N minutes of *trading* time' operation (a naive wall-clock `+ timedelta` would incorrectly cross session/day boundaries for a wide long_term interval), which is exactly the precision `TimeframeInterval.approx_trading_minutes` already documents as deliberately not attempting ('adequate for this guideline-strength comparison, not a precise calendar computation'). Alternative (2) was rejected for the same reason plus one more: `TimeframeTriple` doesn't guarantee any leg's width evenly divides another's (e.g. a 7-minute short_term leg against a 25-minute intermediate leg), so 'fully elapsed' isn't even well-defined at every boundary without further judgment calls of its own -- unwarranted complexity for a feature this task's own `description` already frames as 'genuinely optional/lower-priority'. The chosen uniform rule also directly extends two already-reviewed precedents rather than inventing a new one: `_long_term_through_bar_date`'s `DAY`/`MINUTE` branch was already built this way by `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine`, explicitly 'ready for this' future use and left unmodified here; and both `analyse_history` (swing mode) and `analyse_history_day_trader` already use a bar's own close as-is for the *driving* leg at each replay step, with no settlement-delay applied there either. Verified the resulting tests genuinely discriminate (not just assert a happy path), per this session's own standing instruction on mutation-testing this feature area: temporarily reverted `analyse_history_day_trader`'s truncation calls to pass the full, untruncated `long_term_ohlcv`/`short_term_ohlcv` straight through (no `_long_term_through_bar_date`/`_short_term_through_bar_date` call) and re-ran `TestAnalyseHistoryDayTrader.test_tide_recomputed_as_of_each_bar_date_not_held_at_todays_value` and `.test_short_term_leg_does_not_leak_a_future_bar_backward_into_an_earlier_replay_point` -- both failed exactly as expected (an early bar's Tide flipped to the full-series BEARISH value; every early bar's Trigger falsely fired on the not-yet-reached crossing bar). Reverted immediately afterward and re-ran to confirm both pass again; `git diff` showed no residual change.

decisions.decision: `analyse_history_day_trader` is a wholly new, separate function in `app.signals.engine` -- not a generic parameter/branch added to the existing `analyse_history()`. It duplicates most of `analyse_history`'s own precompute-and-slice structure (the twelve intermediate-leg indicator series, the divergence swing cache, the Kangaroo Tail cache, computed once over the full `intermediate_ohlcv` and sliced per bar), adapted to also precompute/slice `long_term_ohlcv`'s EMA(13)/MACD-Histogram and truncate `short_term_ohlcv` per bar. `analyse()` itself gained one small, additive, default-preserving change: a new private `_short_term_ohlcv_already_clean` escape-hatch parameter (mirroring the pre-existing `_daily_ohlcv_already_clean`), so `analyse_history_day_trader`'s own hot loop doesn't redundantly re-clean `short_term_ohlcv` on every one of potentially thousands of calls the way `analyse()`'s public contract otherwise requires.
decisions.rationale: Matches `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-signal-engine`'s own explicitly stated regression-risk posture for this whole feature area ('extremely careful... regression risk here is real, not hypothetical') -- swing mode's `analyse_history` is this app's own production-critical, already-reviewed chart-overlay implementation, and every existing test/caller of it must remain provably untouched; a new, separate function achieves that with zero risk of an accidental swing-mode regression, at the accepted cost of the two functions' precompute blocks being structurally near-identical. Threading a third, generic helper through both call sites was considered and rejected: with exactly two callers (unlikely to grow a third any time soon, since day-trader mode and swing mode are this app's only two `TradingMode`s by design) and `analyse_history`'s own precompute block already carrying extensive inline commentary earned through real review scrutiny (a documented O(range_size x history_length) -> O(history_length) fix, itself the subject of a dedicated `TestAnalyseHistoryPerformance` test class), the indirection cost of a shared helper wasn't judged worth it versus the small, contained duplication. The `_short_term_ohlcv_already_clean` addition to `analyse()` was judged in scope (not deferred) because leaving it out would silently reintroduce the exact O(range_size)-repeated-`dropna`-scan cost `_daily_ohlcv_already_clean` exists to eliminate for `daily_ohlcv` -- and a walk-forward intraday replay is, if anything, more likely to hit thousands of bars than swing mode's own daily cadence ever is, making this optimization matter at least as much here.
